investigations.title: Why equal counts need unbounded memory
Recover after a known hole
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2–3: P1 with the printed key; match the two surviving entries. Grades 4–5: P2's shortest-key question. Allow 15–25 minutes. Requirements: ordered positions, two counter faces, and comparing rows; no arithmetic beyond counting entries.

investigations.title: Detect damage with a check counter
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2–3 can make rows and test flips after the printed pairing example. Grades 4–5 can classify all distinct flip counts. Allow 15–25 minutes. Requirements: pairing/evenness; count to 5; no binary arithmetic notation.

investigations.title: Locate a change; investigate invisible damage
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2–3 start with P5's visible row/column checks; Grades 4–5 continue to minimum invisible damage and two-flip ambiguity. Allow 20–40 minutes or a whole return visit. Requirements: unchanged4-by-4 orientation, completing each check, and tracking two conditions at once. Adult can mark odd rows/columns at first while the child chooses the intersection.

investigations.title: Pairwise sharing and complement bounds
investigations.entry_detail: P1 is the concrete selection entry for grades 2-3; P2 distinguishes pairwise from whole-family intersection. P3's universal bound is a grades 4-5 continuation. Count cards, not repeated occurrences of symbols. Allow 15-30 minutes.

investigations.title: Reconstruct a rule from its minimal triggers
investigations.entry_detail: P4 uses the printed input/containment/output convention. Grades 2-3 can test every physical card; grades 4-5 can explain P6's guarantee and edge cases. Requirements: containment and one recoverable works/fails catalog. Allow 20-35 minutes.

investigations.title: Nested pairs allowed; triples forbidden
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 can select and challenge physical collections; grades 4-5 can adapt the base chain certificate to two seats per chain. Entry gate: a nested pair is legal here and three distinct nested cards are not. Allow 20-35 minutes or a return visit.

investigations.title: Wandering tokens and exact expected scores
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 can choose fairly and record terminal scores. Grades 4-5 can derive exact values from the first move. Allow 20-30 minutes, including at least the twelve A walks and twelve B walks requested. Adults may scribe while children draw and move.

investigations.title: Cycles and a change in the update rule
investigations.entry_detail: P2-3 have whole-number concrete entries for grades 2-3. P4 is a grades 4-5 or fraction-ready return. Allow 20-35 minutes. The gate is simultaneous replacement from one old board; adults can label positions while children make the new stacks.

investigations.title: Find the least-rough landscape
investigations.entry_detail: Use square drawings or tiles with grades 2-3; grades 4-5 can explain a certificate covering all choices. Whole-number inputs 0-6 and squared areas are the only student prerequisites. Allow 20-35 minutes; pairs can share case checks.

investigations.title: Contact two walls in a prescribed order
investigations.entry_detail: Ready grades 2-3 can trace and fold with an adult; grades 4-5 can explain the length certificate. Gate: lower then upper is a different action from upper then lower. Allow 20-35 minutes, possibly an entire return visit.

investigations.title: Find a new optimum inside allowed windows
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 can slide string contacts along the two heavy windows; grades 4-5 can explain why their endpoints control every competitor. Gate: the light remainder of the line is not a legal contact. Allow 15-25 minutes.

investigations.title: Shortest routes around a rectangle
investigations.entry_detail: Concrete string entry suits grades 2-3 and selected K-1 oral work; proof of all possible routes is a grades 4-5 return. Gate: obstacle edges may be followed here. Allow 20-30 minutes.

investigations.title: Keep a target using the fewest dots
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 can physically remove markers and redraw the filled region. Grades 4-5 can prove the at-most-three fact and audit no-pair evidence. Allow 20-30 minutes. The target remains fixed while supporting dots change.

investigations.title: A line that separates two fixed groups
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 can try a ruler line and redraw each group's filled segment. Grades 4-5 can explain why the crossing defeats every line. Allow 15-25 minutes; reading is the only textual prerequisite.

investigations.title: One common point for three groups
investigations.entry_detail: P4 is a concrete line entry for grades 2-3; P5 adds a spatial construction. P6's complete impossibility argument is a grades 4-5 return. Count labels and retain three groups, not three pairwise intersection marks. Allow 20-35 minutes or more than one visit.

investigations.title: Select part of the order
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 can construct a smallest-card machine and test the printed lower-half machine. Grades 4-5 can defend their guarantees. Requirements: only fixed dotted endpoints compare; output lanes not requested by the goal may remain unordered. Allow 20-35 minutes.

investigations.title: Merge two already sorted pairs
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 can operate two physical sorted trays and test all six legal inputs. Grades 4-5 can explain the three-bar minimum. Gate: each pair is sorted before the machine starts. Allow 15-25 minutes.

investigations.title: Preserve the order of equal cards
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 can operate tagged cards and read A-before-B from lane order. Grades 4-5 can explain the invariant for any neighbor-only machine. Requirements: tags are identifiers, not comparison keys; ties never swap. Allow 20-30 minutes.

investigations.title: Three-way champion
investigations.entry_detail: Compare one visible triple, then let pairs choose how to assemble complete cases. Grades 2-3 can share the 27 cases across a table; Grades 4-5 can count by the potential winning card. Allow 15-25 minutes or continue on a later visit.

investigations.title: Totals can change an advantage
investigations.entry_detail: P2 starts with actual replacement draws and sums, then sorting the nine outcome cards per deck. P3 requires keeping frequencies or distinct physical cards visible. Allow 20-40 minutes; the exact comparisons may be a whole return visit.

investigations.title: Hide the choice; equalize its risks
investigations.entry_detail: Play legal independent rounds before calculating. Every label bag is nonempty; an individual label may have zero slips. Grades 2-3 can test bags and compare pooled exact scores; Grades 4-5 can explain why no bag beats one against every fixed opponent. Allow 20-40 minutes and return for the proof.

investigations.title: An extra shadow can still hide a difference
investigations.entry_detail: Begin by placing three counters with one in every row/column. A younger child can find and compare two actual pictures; an older group can assemble the six-picture catalog and establish completeness. Allow 15-30 minutes.

investigations.title: Choose questions as evidence arrives
investigations.entry_detail: Play P2 with all candidates visible and retain replies by covering or marking candidate cards. P3 changes only when cells are chosen. Reading support is routine; children should retain the choices. Allow 20-40 minutes, with exact minima as return work.

investigations.title: Counts that cannot fit
investigations.entry_detail: Try each printed board with real counters. Allow 15-30 minutes. Counting to three is enough to begin; exact impossibility requires pointing to forced cells or capacity, not simply reporting an unsuccessful attempt.

investigations.title: A shared fence belongs to both rooms
investigations.entry_detail: Make two side-connected rooms with eight R and eight B tiles. Children choose divisions; adults can place edge markers or record counts. Allow 20-35 minutes. General identity and the lower-bound proof are upper return routes.

investigations.title: Corners remember holes
investigations.entry_detail: Build the printed shapes and point to every corner on both outside and hole loops. Count to eight is enough to begin. Allow 20-30 minutes. A turning explanation can occupy another visit with a direction marker.

investigations.title: From footprint to exposed cube surface
investigations.entry_detail: Build and inspect the three eight-cube structures in P4 before equations. Grade labels are approximate: keeping touching faces covered and bottoms included is the real gate. Allow 25-40 minutes; equal-height and terrain rules are rich return work.

investigations.title: Lowest score is not always stable
investigations.entry_detail: Build candidates and attach their two rank numbers to each pair. Grades 2-3 can pool the six cases; older children can certify both minima. Allow 20-30 minutes. Rank score and a blocker are separate records about the same unchanged matching.

investigations.title: Partners can change; matched objects cannot
investigations.entry_detail: P2 uses small omitted-choice profiles and visible unpaired objects. P4 lets children design lists and seek a counterexample. Allow 20-40 minutes; the general proof can be a separate upper return conversation using alternating colored links.

investigations.title: One group may have no stable pairing
investigations.entry_detail: Four identical-style tokens permit every within-group pair. Keep one candidate matching fixed while testing both wishes. Allow 15-30 minutes. A child can explain nonexistence by exhausting three drawings, without a matching algorithm.

investigations.title: One crease must satisfy every alignment
investigations.entry_detail: Trace the printed diagrams exactly onto thin paper, rather than copying approximately. Bring the P side onto Q's side; test R/S at the same fold. Keep T fixed when requested. Allow 20-30 minutes; distance/bisector explanations are an upper continuation.

investigations.title: Directions and static layer order
investigations.entry_detail: P2 uses actual connected three-panel strips; keep B's original front up for the top-to-bottom word. P3 asks only for noncrossing static side views. Allow 20-40 minutes and return for completeness; use movable letter cards when sorting is the mathematics.

investigations.title: One punch, many reflected centers
investigations.entry_detail: Use actual thin squares and an adult-assisted punch after the printed single-fold bridge. Children choose positions and compare unfoldings; exact inverse tests are older return work. Allow 20-35 minutes per branch. Keep the top-right quarter underneath as specified.

investigations.title: Count the order, not just the combination
investigations.entry_detail: Arrange rods with the fixed left end, then make movable word records. K-1 can compare two arrangements; Grades 2-3 organize small complete lists; Grades 4-5 explain the last-rod rule. Allow 20-35 minutes and return for eighteen or the general count.

investigations.title: A finite build has a complementary remainder
investigations.entry_detail: Use only the sealed seven-rod kit and two visible lanes. Children choose used rods; unused rods externalize the complement. Counting/alignment is enough to start. Allow 20-30 minutes; a general correspondence is older return work.

investigations.title: A redundant rod can still save pieces
investigations.entry_detail: Use three separate unlimited toolkits, not cumulative additions. Try substitutions and short minimum-piece builds first. Allow 20-40 minutes; proofs of all new targets and minimum counts can be return work.

investigations.title: A kit that survives any one loss
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 start P1 with physical removal; Grades 4-5 continue P2-3 after reliable testing. Allow 20-35 minutes. An adult may record the nine P1 balances while children choose them.

investigations.title: Find a hidden mass with comparisons
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 maintain candidate cards while a partner supplies exact outcomes. Grades 4-5 explain the bound. Allow 20-30 minutes. No physical mass estimation or guessing is part of the rule.

investigations.title: All weights in equal teams
investigations.entry_detail: K-1 can use P6's first kit orally; Grades 2-3 compare the four kits; Grades 4-5 defend P7 completeness. Allow 15-30 minutes, longer for children inventing their own partition challenges.

investigations.title: Two lookouts and common blind spots
investigations.suitable_bands_and_readiness: K-5 concrete sightline entry; 2-5 row rules
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 test targets with thread and record B/1/0 in one table. Grades 4-5 explain the infinite row claim. Allow 20-30 minutes. The lookup codes are categories, not arithmetic counts to be added.

investigations.title: Visible edges and empty triangles
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 mark boundary/interior dots and use copied shapes to compare areas. Grades 4-5 continue to P4's impossibility explanation. Allow 25-40 minutes or a return visit. Formal determinants and a proof of Pick's theorem are not child prerequisites.

investigations.title: Grow neighboring visible directions
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 add and insert physical cards after the worked visual. Grades 4-5 explain why hidden (4,2) is excluded and how any positive coprime target is found. Allow 25-45 minutes, with a separate return for the general rule.

investigations.title: Biggest squares versus fewest squares
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 keep two physical tilings and compare counts. Grades 4-5 defend P2's minimum. Allow 25-40 minutes. Pairwise fit arguments can be shown with paper squares; equations are optional.

investigations.title: Allowed square sizes and hidden obstructions
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 attempt all three boards using only side-2/3 pieces. Grades 4-5 turn failure into boundary or packing explanations. Allow 20-35 minutes. Adult may write area counts while children arrange tiles.

investigations.title: Rebuild a size-free recipe
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 draw or assemble from groups once the count convention is understood. Grades 4-5 explain scaling and unique ratio. Allow 20-35 minutes or a full return. No fraction-expression fluency is required.

investigations.title: Mirror twins and two matching rules
investigations.suitable_bands_and_readiness: K-5 oral overlay entry; shared sheet 2-5
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 build and compare the six references with an overlay; Grades 4-5 explain the gap distinction. Allow 20-30 minutes. A letter naming a reference is not a permanent marked bead.

investigations.title: Different neighbors, including the closing pair
investigations.entry_detail: K-1 oral entry can attempt the two-kind rings; Grades 2-3 build the six three-kind classes; Grades 4-5 defend completeness. Allow 20-35 minutes or a separate visit. A partner checks adjacent pairs and the closing pair.

investigations.title: Every short code as a local window
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 start P4-5 with four cards, then P6 when wraparound reading is reliable. Grades 4-5 seek P7 completeness and the shortest bound. Allow 25-45 minutes, with three-window work as a return.

investigations.title: Choose how many flips remain
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 build for one, two or three matching flips and let partners test. Grades 4-5 explain the four-flip impossibility. Allow 20-35 minutes. A whole turn is identity, not an additional nonidentity motion.

investigations.title: Repair a specified motion with fewest changes
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 compare opposite pairs for P3; Grades 4-5 use pairs/cycles for P4. Allow 25-40 minutes. Restore the exact printed start between targets and count changed spots, not moves of the overlay.

investigations.title: Stack symmetric layers and compare common motions
investigations.entry_detail: Grades 2-3 retain both layer identities; Grades 4-5 explain intersection. Allow 20-35 minutes. Adult may read; the child must control marks and comparisons rather than merely watch a stack being made.
